section_desc: In this Code: 'employee' means any person employed on wages by an establishment directly or through contractor; 'employer' means any person who employs one or more persons directly or through contractor; 'wages' means all remuneration whether by way of salaries, allowances or otherwise, expressed in terms of money or capable of being so expressed and includes basic pay, dearness allowance, retaining allowance — but excludes employer's contribution to PF/ESI, house rent allowance, overtime allowance, bonus, commission; 'floor wage' means minimum wage fixed by Central Government for different geographical areas.

section_title: Prohibition of discrimination on ground of gender in matters of wages
section_desc: No employer shall pay to an employee at a rate less favourable than that at which remuneration is paid by him to an employee of the other gender for performing the same work or work of a similar nature. This provision applies irrespective of any other legislation. It subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 into the Code on Wages.

The appropriate Government shall fix minimum rates of wages payable to employees in scheduled employments. Different minimum rates may be fixed for different categories of workers — unskilled, semi-skilled, skilled, highly skilled; and for different geographical areas. The Central Government shall fix a floor wage taking into account living standards of workers. No minimum rate of wages shall be fixed or revised for any employment for which a national minimum wage has been fixed by the Central Government if the State's minimum is lower than national floor.

section_title: Fixing hours for normal working day etc.
section_desc: In regard to any scheduled employment minimum rates of wages in respect of which have been fixed under this Code, the appropriate Government may fix the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day — not more than eight hours per day; the number of days of rest to be allowed; provision for work on days of rest and payment of wages at overtime rate — at least twice the normal rate.

All wages shall be paid in current coin or currency notes or by cheque or by crediting in the bank account of the employee or by electronic mode. The wages of every person employed in an establishment shall be paid: where less than 1000 persons are employed — before expiry of seventh day after last day of wage period; where 1000 or more persons — before expiry of tenth day. Wages for dismissed/removed employee must be paid within two working days.

section_title: Penalties for offences under Code on Wages
section_desc: If any employer pays to any employee less than the amount due to him under the provisions of this Code, he shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees for first contravention; one lakh rupees for second contravention; and two lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions. If the offence relates to deduction from wages, penalty is fifty thousand rupees. Compounding of offences is permitted for first offenders.

In this Code: 'industry' means any systematic activity carried on by co-operation between an employer and worker (whether or not employing capital) for the production, supply or distribution of goods or services with a view to satisfy human wants or wishes; 'industrial dispute' means any dispute or difference between employers and employers, or between employers and workers, or between workers and workers, which is connected with the employment or non-employment or the terms of employment or with the conditions of labour, of any person; 'workman' means any person including an apprentice, employed in any industry to do any manual, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work.

No worker employed in an industrial establishment shall go on strike and no employer of an industrial establishment shall declare a lock-out in breach of contract: without giving notice of strike or lock-out as the case may be to the other party — sixty days notice in public utility services, fourteen days in others; within fourteen days of giving such notice; before the expiry of the date of strike specified in the notice; during the pendency of conciliation proceedings; during the pendency of proceedings before a Tribunal; during any period in which a settlement or award is in operation in respect of the said dispute.

No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until: the workman has been given one month's notice in writing with reasons or wages in lieu; the workman has been paid retrenchment compensation equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service; notice of retrenchment is given to appropriate Government one month before. Establishments with 300+ workers need prior permission from appropriate government for retrenchment.

An employer who intends to close down an undertaking of an industrial establishment shall serve, at least ninety days before the date on which the intended closure is to become effective, a notice in the prescribed manner on the appropriate Government stating clearly the reasons for the intended closure of the undertaking. No such notice shall be necessary for an undertaking employing less than fifty workmen, or an undertaking set up for the construction of buildings, bridges, roads, canals, dams or for other construction work.

act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section_desc: In this Code: 'establishment' means any place where any industry, trade, business, manufacture, or occupation is carried on; 'factory' means any premises where ten or more workers are working with aid of power or twenty or more workers without aid of power; 'hazardous process' means any process which is likely to cause material impairment to the health of workers engaged in or connected therewith; 'occupational disease' means any disease specified in the Third Schedule contracted by a worker employed in any process involving risk of such disease.

act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section_desc: Every employer shall provide and maintain a work environment which is safe and without risk to the health of the workers; ensure that work systems are such as not to expose workers to health hazards; provide workers with safety gear and personal protective equipment as required; ensure adequate first-aid facilities; undertake health surveillance of workers employed in hazardous processes; report any accident, dangerous occurrence, occupational disease; maintain register of accidents and dangerous occurrences.

act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section_desc: Every worker shall: take reasonable care of his own health and safety and of other persons who may be affected by his acts or omissions; comply with such requirements as are imposed on him by or under this Code; co-operate with the employer in complying with the provisions of this Code; refrain from wilfully misusing or interfering with or damaging anything provided in the interest of health, safety and working conditions; not wilfully or recklessly interfere with or misuse any appliance, convenience or other thing provided for securing the health, safety or welfare of workers.

act: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section_desc: No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than forty-eight hours in any week; for more than nine hours in any day. Worker who works overtime (beyond 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week) is entitled to overtime wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages. Maximum overtime: 100 hours per quarter. A worker may not be required to work continuously for more than five hours without a rest interval of at least half an hour.

In this Code: 'aggregator' means a digital intermediary or a market place for a buyer or user of a service to connect with the seller or the service provider; 'building and other construction worker' means any person employed for wages to do any building or other construction work; 'gig worker' means a person who performs work or participates in a work arrangement and earns from such activities outside of traditional employer-employee relationship; 'platform worker' means a person engaged in or undertaking platform work; 'unorganised worker' means a home based worker, self employed worker or a daily wage worker.

The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, frame a scheme to be called the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme for the establishment of provident funds under this Code for employees or for any class of employees and specify the establishments or class of establishments to which the said scheme shall apply. The employer's contribution shall be 12% of wages; employee's contribution shall be equal to employer's contribution. Central Government may fix higher rate.

The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, frame a scheme to be called the Employees' State Insurance Scheme for providing certain benefits to employees in case of sickness, maternity and employment injury. Every factory or establishment to which this Code applies shall be registered with the ESIC. Contribution rates: employer — 3.25% of wages; employee — 0.75% of wages. Workers earning less than Rs 21,000 per month are covered.

Gratuity shall be payable to an employee on the termination of his employment after he has rendered continuous service for not less than five years: on his superannuation; on his retirement or resignation; on his death or disablement due to accident or disease. Amount: fifteen days' wages for every completed year of service. The five-year condition is not applicable on death or disablement. Maximum gratuity payable: Rs 20 lakh. Fixed-term contract employees eligible for gratuity on proportionate basis.

section_title: Social security for gig workers and platform workers
section_desc: The Central Government shall frame suitable social security schemes for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age protection, crèche facility and any other benefit as may be determined by the Central Government. The aggregator shall contribute between 1% to 2% of annual turnover of the platform towards social security fund for gig and platform workers. This is a first in India — formal social security for the gig economy.

act: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
section_desc: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, frame a scheme to be called the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme for the establishment of provident funds under this Act for employees or for any class of employees and specify the establishments or class of establishments to which the said scheme shall apply. The scheme shall specify the rate of contribution, the persons to whom contributions are to be paid, conditions for membership and benefits payable from the Fund.

act: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
section_desc: The employer shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of twelve percent per annum or at such higher rate as may be specified in the scheme on any amount due from him under this Act from the date on which the amount has become so due till the date of its actual payment. Where interest is collected under this Act, the same shall be credited to the fund. The interest on delayed payment is penal in nature.

act: The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
section_desc: Where an employer makes default in the payment of any contribution to the Fund, the Pension Scheme or the Insurance Scheme, or in the transfer of accumulations required to be transferred, or in the payment of any charges payable under any other provision of this Act, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner or such officer as may be authorised by the Central Government, may recover from the employer by way of penalty such damages, not exceeding the amount of arrears, as may be specified.
chapter_title: Recovery of Money due from Employers

section_desc: In this Act: 'benefit period' means a period for which insured persons are entitled to certain cash benefits under the Act; 'confinement' means labour resulting in the issue of a living child, or labour after twenty-six weeks of pregnancy resulting in the issue of a child whether alive or dead; 'contributory conditions' means the conditions prescribed with reference to the payment of contributions; 'employment injury' means a personal injury to an employee caused by accident or an occupational disease arising out of and in the course of employment in a factory or establishment to which this Act applies.

section_title: Principal employer to pay contributions in the first instance
section_desc: The principal employer shall pay in respect of every employee, whether directly employed by him or by or through an immediate employer, both the employer's contribution and the employee's contribution. The principal employer may recover from an immediate employer the employer's contribution in respect of employees employed by or through such immediate employer. The contribution shall be paid on wages, not on other allowances or perquisites.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, the insured persons, their dependants or certain other persons shall be entitled to the following benefits: periodical payments to an insured person in case of his incapacity for work resulting from sickness; periodical payments to an insured woman in case of confinement or miscarriage; periodical payments to an insured person for disablement resulting from an employment injury; medical benefit to an insured person and his family; funeral expenses; rehabilitation allowance.

In this Act: 'adult' means a person who has completed his eighteenth year of age; 'adolescent' means a person who has completed his fifteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year; 'child' means a person who has not completed his fifteenth year of age; 'factory' means any premises including the precincts thereof wherein ten or more workers are working, or were working on any day of the preceding twelve months, and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on with the aid of power; 'hazardous process' means any process listed in Schedule 1.

Every factory shall be kept clean and free from effluvia arising from any drain, privy or other nuisance. In particular: accumulation of dirt and refuse shall be removed daily by sweeping or by any other effective method; the floor of every workroom shall be cleaned at least once a week; where the floor is liable to become wet, effective drainage shall be provided; all inside walls and partitions, all ceilings shall be repainted or varnished once in every five years.

There shall in every factory be provided and maintained so as to be readily accessible during all working hours first-aid boxes or cupboards equipped with the prescribed contents, and the number of such boxes or cupboards to be provided and maintained shall not be less than one for every one hundred and fifty workers ordinarily employed at any one time in the factory. Each first-aid box shall be kept in the charge of a responsible person who holds a certificate in first-aid treatment.

No adult worker shall be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than forty-eight hours in any week. Where an adult worker works for more than nine hours on any day or more than forty-eight hours in any week, he shall, in respect of overtime work, be entitled to wages at the rate of twice his ordinary rate of wages. No adult worker shall work more than a total of fifty hours of overtime in any quarter.

section_title: Prohibition of employment of young children
section_desc: No child who has not completed his fourteenth year of age shall be required or allowed to work in any factory. No child who has not completed his fifteenth year shall be required or allowed to work in any factory unless a certificate of fitness granted by a certifying surgeon is in his custody. An adolescent who has obtained a certificate of fitness for work in a factory may work as an adult in such factory between 6 AM and 7 PM.

In this Act: 'mine' means any excavation where any operation for the purpose of searching for or obtaining minerals has been or is being carried on, and includes all borings, bore holes, oil wells and accessory crude conditioning plants; 'owner' means any person who is the immediate proprietor or lessee or occupier of the mine; 'agent' means any person appointed by the owner of a mine to act as a representative responsible for the working of the mine; 'manager' means the person appointed to be the manager of a mine under section 17.

No person employed in a mine shall be required or allowed to work therein more than six days in any week. An adult person is entitled to at least one day of rest per week. Overtime work in mines is not allowed except under emergency situations with prior permission of Inspector of Mines. Hours of work not to exceed eight hours per day in underground mines.

In this Act: 'environment' includes water, air and land and the inter-relationship which exists among and between water, air and land, and human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organism and property; 'environmental contaminant' means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance present in the environment in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to environment; 'environmental pollution' means the presence in the environment of any environmental pollutant; 'hazardous substance' means any substance or preparation which, by reason of its chemical or physico-chemical properties is liable to cause harm to human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms, property or the environment.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law but subject to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, in the exercise of its powers and performance of its functions under this Act, issue directions in writing to any person, officer or any authority and such person, officer or authority shall be bound to comply with such directions. Such directions may include closure, prohibition or regulation of any industry, operation or process; stoppage or regulation of the supply of electricity, water or any other service.
chapter_title: General Powers of the Central Government

section_title: Persons carrying on industry etc. not to allow emission or discharge of environmental pollutants in excess of standards
section_desc: No person carrying on any industry, operation or process shall discharge or emit or permit to be discharged or emitted any environmental pollutant in excess of such standards as may be prescribed. Where the discharge of any environmental pollutant in excess of the prescribed standards occurs or is apprehended to occur due to any accident or other unforeseen act or event, the person responsible shall be bound to prevent or mitigate the environmental pollution caused as a result thereof.
chapter_title: General Powers of the Central Government

act: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
section_desc: In this Act: 'Board' means the Central Board or a State Board; 'outlet' means any conduit, pipe, channel, well, drain, sewer, or any other means whereby the discharge of sewage or trade effluent or any other polluting matter including silt, ash and refuse is made; 'pollution' means such contamination of water or such alteration of the physical, chemical or biological properties of water or such discharge of any sewage or trade effluent or of any other liquid, gaseous or solid substance into water as may be detrimental to the life and health of human beings or animals or plants.

act: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
section_title: Restrictions on new outlets and new discharges
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this section, no person shall, without the previous consent of the State Board, establish or take any steps to establish any industry, operation or process, or any treatment and disposal system or any extension or addition thereto, which is likely to discharge sewage or trade effluent into a stream or well or sewer or on land. The Board shall not refuse to grant consent unreasonably.
chapter_title: Prevention and Control of Water Pollution

act: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
section_desc: In this Act: 'air pollutant' means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance including noise present in the atmosphere in such concentration as may be or tend to be injurious to human beings or other living creatures or plants or property or environment; 'air pollution' means the presence in the atmosphere of any air pollutant; 'industry' means any industry specified in Schedule I to this Act; 'stack' means a chimney, flue, conduit, duct, opening or other structure through which air pollutants pass into the atmosphere.

act: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
section_title: Restrictions on use of certain industrial plants
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this section, no person shall, without the previous consent of the State Pollution Control Board, establish or operate any industrial plant in an air pollution control area. An application for consent shall be made in the prescribed form. The State Board shall have powers to grant, refuse or revoke consent and to impose conditions. Every person operating an industrial plant shall comply with standards for emission of air pollutants.
chapter_title: Prevention and Control of Air Pollution

section_desc: In this Act: 'applicant' means a person who makes an application to the Tribunal; 'environment' has the same meaning as in the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; 'substantial question relating to environment' means a question that relates directly to the enforcement of any legal right relating to environment or effective implementation of any of the environmental statutes under Schedule I; 'Tribunal' means the National Green Tribunal established under section 3.

The Central Government shall, by notification, establish, with effect from such date as may be specified therein, a Tribunal to be known as the National Green Tribunal to exercise the jurisdiction, powers and authority conferred on such Tribunal by or under this Act. The Principal Bench shall be at New Delhi. The Central Government may, by notification, establish Benches of the Tribunal at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. The Tribunal shall consist of a full-time Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members.
chapter_title: Establishment and Constitution of the Tribunal

section_desc: The Tribunal shall, while passing any order or decision or award, apply the principles of sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle. Polluter pays principle: the person responsible for pollution must bear the cost of remediation and compensation. Precautionary principle: where there is a threat of serious or irreversible environmental damage, lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures.
chapter_title: Jurisdiction, Powers, and Proceedings of the Tribunal

section_desc: In this Act: 'animal' includes amphibians, birds, mammals, and reptiles and their young, and in the case of birds and reptiles, their eggs; 'hunting' includes killing or poisoning of any wild animal, capturing, coursing, snaring, trapping, driving or baiting any wild or captive animal; 'protected area' means a national park, a sanctuary, a conservation reserve or a community reserve; 'Schedule' means a Schedule appended to this Act — Schedule I animals have highest protection.

No person shall hunt any wild animal specified in Schedules I, II, III and IV except as provided under section 11 and section 12. Hunting means: killing or poisoning; capturing; coursing, snaring, trapping, driving or baiting; attempting to do any of the above. Section 11 allows killing in special circumstances (imminent threat to human life). Section 12 allows grant of special licences.

Whenever it appears to the State Government that an area, whether it is a sanctuary or not, is, by reason of its ecological, faunal, floral, geomorphological or zoological association or importance, needed to be constituted as a national park for the purpose of protecting, propagating or developing wildlife therein or its environment, it may, by notification, declare its intention to constitute such area as a national park. Once declared, no commercial exploitation is allowed in a national park.
chapter_title: Sanctuaries, National Parks, and Closed Areas

section_title: Prohibition of trade or commerce in trophies, animal articles etc. derived from certain animals
section_desc: No person shall engage in trade or commerce in any animal article, trophy, captive animal or meat derived from any of the animals specified in Schedules I and II except under and in accordance with a licence granted under section 44. Any contravention shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than three years but may extend to seven years and fine not less than ten thousand rupees.
chapter_title: Trade and Commerce in Wild Animals, Animal Articles and Trophies

section_title: Prohibition on biological resources without approval
section_desc: No person who is a citizen of India, or a body corporate, association or organisation which is registered in India, shall obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or for commercial utilisation or for bio-survey and bio-utilisation except after obtaining prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority. Non-citizens and foreign companies need prior approval for any access to Indian biological resources.

Nothing in section 3 shall apply to collaborative research projects between Indian and foreign institutions that: are approved by the Central Government; do not involve transfer of biological resources or knowledge associated thereto occurring in India outside India for commercial purposes; involves a collaborative research project approved under guidelines issued by the Central Government. Indian institutions must be equally involved.

The National Biodiversity Authority shall, while granting approvals under this Act, ensure that terms and conditions subject to which approval is granted secure equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of accessed biological resources, their by-products, innovations and practices associated with their use and applications and knowledge relating thereto in accordance with mutually agreed terms between the person applying for such approval, the local bodies concerned, and the benefit claimers.

section_title: Restriction on dereservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purpose
section_desc: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force in a State, no State Government or other authority shall make, except with the prior approval of the Central Government, any order directing that any reserved forest shall cease to be reserved; that any forest land or any portion thereof may be used for any non-forest purpose; that any forest land or any portion thereof may be assigned by way of lease or otherwise to any private person; that any forest land or any portion thereof may be cleared of trees for the purposes of reafforestation.

Whoever contravenes or abets the contravention of any of the provisions of section 2 shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a period which may extend to fifteen days. Any State Government or other authority who violates section 2 without Central Government approval commits an offence. Violation also results in the Collector demanding restoration of the diverted forest land.

Local bodies shall be responsible for developing infrastructure for segregation, collection, storage, transportation, processing and disposal of plastic waste, either on their own or by engaging agencies or producers. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) makes producers responsible for collection and recycling of plastic waste they generate. Producers must register with the State Pollution Control Board and submit annual reports on plastic waste management.

The producer shall be responsible for Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for e-waste generated from end-of-life of its products. Producers must register on EPR portal of CPCB; set targets for collection of e-waste; ensure collection through registered dismantlers and recyclers; submit annual reports. EPR targets: 60% of the weight of electrical and electronic equipment placed on the market in previous year by 2023; increasing to 70% by 2025.

In this Act: 'disaster' means a catastrophe, mishap, calamity or grave occurrence in any area, arising from natural or manmade causes, or by accident or negligence which results in substantial loss of life or human suffering or damage to, and destruction of, property, or damage to, or degradation of, environment, and is of such a nature or magnitude as to be beyond the coping capacity of the community of the affected area; 'disaster management' means a continuous and integrated process of planning, organising, coordinating and implementing measures which are necessary or expedient for prevention of disaster or mitigation or preparedness and capacity building.

section_title: Establishment of National Disaster Management Authority
section_desc: There shall be established a National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The Prime Minister of India shall be the Chairperson of the National Authority. The National Authority shall consist of the Chairperson and such number of other members, not exceeding nine. The National Authority shall lay down the policies on disaster management; approve the National Plan; approve plans prepared by Ministries; lay down guidelines to be followed by State Authorities in drawing up State Plans.

In this Act: 'carrier' means a person engaged in the business of collecting, storing, forwarding or delivering goods by road; 'consignee' means the person to whom the goods are to be delivered; 'consignor' means the person by whom the goods are sent or to be sent; 'goods receipt' means the receipt issued by the carrier for the goods received from the consignor acknowledging receipt of goods; 'transit' means period from receipt of goods at consignor's premises to delivery at consignee's premises.

'Accident' means an accident involving motor vehicles; 'Gross Vehicle Weight' means the total weight of a vehicle and load certified and registered; 'Heavy goods vehicle' means any goods carriage the gross vehicle weight exceeds 12000 kgs; 'Light motor vehicle' means a transport vehicle or omnibus with gross vehicle weight or unladen weight not exceeding 7500 kgs; 'Motor vehicle' or 'vehicle' means any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted for use upon roads; 'Private service vehicle' means a motor vehicle not a transport vehicle.

section_title: Automated testing and fitness of vehicles
section_desc: Every motor vehicle including a transport vehicle shall be so maintained that it conforms to the prescribed standards so as to ensure the safety of the public. The testing of motor vehicles shall be automated and computerised. The certificate of fitness shall be issued on the basis of such automated testing. All vehicles shall be subject to automated fitness testing at Automated Testing Stations (ATS). Vehicles failing the test shall not be permitted on public roads.

Whoever drives or causes or allows to be driven in any public place any goods vehicle with gross vehicle weight exceeding the registered gross vehicle weight of the vehicle shall be punishable with: first offence — fine of Rs 20,000 plus Rs 2,000 per ton of excess load; subsequent offences — fine of Rs 20,000 plus Rs 2,000 per ton of excess load. Overloaded vehicles may be detained until excess load is removed.
